newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch bourse to set up market for young companies.
newsitem.headline: Dutch bourse to set up market for young companies.

text.p: The Amsterdam Stock Exchange said on Thursday it would set up a new market where shares in young and fast growing companies can be traded.

The market, which will be called "New Market Amsterdam", will offer the opportunity for an official listing of companies which cannot be quoted on the bourse's main market because they do not yet have a track record.

"By setting up this market, Amsterdam will be linked with the so called Euro Marche, the intended cooperation pact of the Paris, Frankfurt and Brussels exchanges," the Amsterdam bourse said in a statement.
It added it expected the new market to start business before the end of this year.
Companies applying for a listing in the new sector are not obliged to have been profitable for a number of years, as is the case with firms seeking a flotation on Amsterdam's main market.

But the bourse said the firms will have the same information duties and the financial institution backing the flotation will have to do a due diligence survey, as is the case with Amsterdam's main market.
The bank or broker leading the flotation will have to act as a "sponsor" and maintain market liquidity for three years after introduction of the company to the new market.
The Amsterdam Stock Exchange said it would publish further details in the coming months.
